title: Soft quarantine + adaptive burst-smoothing for tenant saturation incidents
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: During the Feb 3rd Dedicated cluster saturation incident we observed sustained tenant-driven token storms that caused eviction cascades and >3x tail latency for paying customers. Root causes include reservation mis-sizing for several legacy tenants, lack of a soft-containment pathway (we immediately evicted pods) and an overly permissive burst policy that allowed short token spikes to exhaust shared burst tokens across the allocation.

Goal: Implement a low-risk mitigation (soft quarantine) + an adaptive burst-smoothing controller to reduce amplification of short spikes and allow graceful degradation without immediate evictions. This ticket covers design, prototype, rollout plan, and post-deploy telemetry validation.

Scope: 1) implement a soft quarantine workflow that marks a tenant as 'quarantined' for up to N minutes when early noisy-neighbor signals are detected (prefix KV pressure, disproportionate GPU utilization, or queue depth growth); 2) implement burst-smoothing algorithm in the admission controller to convert short high-rate bursts into smoothed ingress allowing token decay and temporary rate shaping; 3) augment reservation telemetry: per-tenant 95/99/99.9th token-per-second distribution, KV cache miss rate, GPU memory stalls; 4) playbook updates and runbook automation to surface quarantine decisions and allow safe manual override.

Success metrics: - Reduce number of hard evictions during similar incidents by >=90% in the Canary cluster within 2 weeks of rollout. - Reduce 99th percentile tail latency for impacted tenants by >=50% during simulated bursts. - Maintain overall throughput within -10% of baseline for healthy tenants.

Acceptance criteria: - E2E tests validating quarantine entry/exit and API visibility. - Canary rollout (10% of traffic) with telemetry dashboards and automated rollback on metric regressions. - Runbook updated and on-call run through completed.

Design trade-offs and rationale: Soft quarantine trades strict isolation for graceful degradation, which helps preserve QoS for most customers while limiting blast radius. Burst-smoothing favors transient latency over eviction-based throughput loss. We avoid immediate hard reservations changes in this ticket to reduce blast risk; rightsizing will be a follow-up once telemetry identifies repeat offenders.
comments: 2025-02-10 Asha Patel: Initial writeup after incident debrief. Attached preliminary telemetry outputs from Grafana (see attachments). Proposing soft quarantine TTL=5m and backoff window=30s as starting point.

2025-02-11 Daniel Kim: Spiked a quick prototype for the quarantine marker in the admission controller branch. See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1427. Prototype toggles enforcement via feature flag 'soft_quarantine_v1'.

2025-02-13 Marisol Ruiz (SRE): Telemetry note: KV cache miss rate correlated strongly with request amplification; noisy tenant T-204 had sustained 72% KV miss and 5x seq length variance. Dash: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/cluster/kv-miss?orgId=1&var-tenant=T-204
2025-02-17 Liam O'Connor (PM): Please ensure Canary plan includes a kill-switch and automated rollback thresholds: evictions >1/min OR 99p latency increase >30% for >10m should trigger rollback.

2025-02-19 Daniel Kim: Implemented burst-smoothing regulator (leaky-bucket token smoothing with adaptive window). Benchmarked in staging: 99p latency down 42% on synthetic spike tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1439

2025-02-21 Asha Patel: Design review notes: - Need to expose quarantine_reason and quarantine_score in per-tenant console pages. - Add audit log entries to avoid stealthy quarantines. - Security review not required for initial telemetry-only flags.
2025-02-24 SRE team: Dry-run in canary (5% of dedicated capacity) scheduled for 2025-03-02. Will collect metrics for two rolling weeks before widening rollout.

2025-03-02 Daniel Kim: Canary rollout started. Early metrics (first 6h): evictions reduced to 0 (baseline 3/hour during simulated tests), overall 99p latency for canary tenants reduced 35%. No manual overrides issued.

2025-03-03 Marisol Ruiz: Noticed a regression in one tenant where smoothing created head-of-line latency for very small requests (<16 tokens). We mitigated by lowering smoothing window for requests <32 tokens. Will keep under observation.

2025-03-03 Asha Patel: Next steps: finalize parameter autotuner (learning rate for smoothing window), complete runbook updates, and schedule 25% rollout after 2025-03-10 subject to metrics stability. Follow-up ticket for reservation rightsizing will be created to avoid scope creep.
